statements: Create prorate.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with two named function exports, prorate(planCents, periodStart, periodEnd, changeDate) and settle(planCents, periodStart, periodEnd, changeDate). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/.

A date argument must be a string that names a real calendar date of the proleptic Gregorian calendar in the exact form YYYY-MM-DD, with a year from 1900 to 2100 inclusive. Any other value is invalid and the function throws a RangeError whose code property is 'E_DATE'.
planCents must be a safe integer from 0 to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER inclusive; -0 is accepted as 0. Any other value is invalid and the function throws a RangeError whose code property is 'E_AMOUNT'.

The billing period is half-open: periodStart is included and periodEnd is excluded. periodStart must be strictly before periodEnd, otherwise the function throws a RangeError whose code property is 'E_PERIOD'.
changeDate must satisfy periodStart <= changeDate <= periodEnd, otherwise the function throws a RangeError whose code property is 'E_RANGE'.

Arguments are checked in a fixed order and the first failing check decides the error: planCents, then periodStart, periodEnd and changeDate in that order (each for format and calendar validity), then the period, then the range of changeDate. An invalid call throws before returning anything.
Days are whole calendar days. totalDays is the number of days in the period; remainingDays is the number of days from changeDate (included) to periodEnd (excluded).
prorate returns planCents * remainingDays / totalDays rounded to the nearest whole cent, with exact halves rounded up, exact for every valid input. The result is a safe integer and never -0.

settle returns an object with the properties credit and charge. charge equals what prorate returns for the same arguments; credit is the part of planCents already used (periodStart included, changeDate excluded) and equals planCents minus charge, so credit + charge equals planCents exactly. Both are safe integers and never -0.
Leap years follow the Gregorian calendar rule.
Both functions are pure: they perform no I/O, read no clock, keep no shared state and do not mutate their arguments.
brief: Implement prorate.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
